teams.heading: Jake White's Fiji trained at Salmo before losing 15-43 to Ireland
teams.body: Dublin junior club De La Salle Palmerston FC, known locally as Salmo, hosted the squad all week, and its director of rugby, Norman Byrne, called the players "the nicest people you’ll ever come across." Fiji moved their captain's run to Kirwan Park rather than the Aviva Stadium, and forwards coach Gert Smal watched on as Josua Tuisova and Jiuta Wainiqolo were on the pitch. They then lost 15-43 to Ireland at the Aviva Stadium on Saturday night.

teams.heading: Will Joseph scores five tries to equal England's Test record
teams.body: Will Joseph's hat-trick came inside 20 minutes of Saturday's 78-15 win over Japan, and a fifth try after the break left him level with Douglas Lambert, Rory Underwood, Josh Lewsey and Henry Arundell as the only England men to score five in a Test. Joseph, 24, won his only previous cap under Eddie Jones in 2022. With Immanuel Feyi-Waboso out for the rest of the tournament, former England wing Chris Ashton told BBC Radio 5 Live that Joseph is "pretty similar" to Feyi-Waboso in how he plays.

teams.heading: Julien Marchand ruled out of Nations Championship; Matthieu Jalibert nears return
teams.body: Hooker Julien Marchand, who felt further tightness in his thigh during the warm-up against South Africa, is ruled out for the rest of the competition, Planet Rugby has confirmed. Peato Mauvaka started in his place, after Marchand had already missed the start of the French camp with a hamstring injury, and Guillaume Cramont becomes France's reserve hooker. Matthieu Jalibert, out since a quadriceps injury in September, is expected at Marcoussis early next week, news Fabien Galthié will welcome given his fly-half options have been decimated by injury.

lead.why: A new France injury event (Marchand out for the rest of the competition) plus Jalibert's return, and it is not a Dupont retelling.

teams.heading: Andy Farrell admitted Ireland made too many errors in beating Fiji
teams.body: Fiji's quick tries from Josua Tuisova and Peceli Yato overturned Tommy O'Brien's early opener, and Ireland trailed briefly before leading 17-15 at the break. They pulled clear in the second half for a 43-15 win, but Farrell was blunt about the start. "There were too many errors from us and we were losing ground, certainly in the first half physically," he told Virgin Media Sport. The result leaves Ireland level on 20 points with England, a point behind France, ahead of South Africa next week.

teams.heading: Garbisi's missed touch-kick sinks Italy as Argentina edge Genoa 19-14
teams.body: Italy led early through Monty Ioane's corner try, but Saturday's match at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris turned on Argentina's second-half tries. Rodrigo Isgró and Mateo Carreras crossed for Argentina, and Italy were awarded a penalty try after Efraín Elías was shown a yellow card for bringing down a maul. Italy pressed against 14 men but kept undermining their attacks with mistakes, and the final act was Paolo Garbisi's missed penalty touch-kick while trying to set up a lineout in a scoring position.

lead.why: It is the only fresh match report on offer, and it turns on an Italy error.

teams.heading: Joey Sharp, who overcame a brain tumour, to deliver Murrayfield match ball
teams.body: Joey Sharp, who is five, will deliver the match ball alongside Commonwealth Games swimmer Archie Goodburn, and Scottish Rugby have arranged for him and his mother, Sam Sharp, to meet the players. It will be his first visit to Murrayfield, and accessible seating has been arranged for the family. Joey was diagnosed with a brain tumour at 11 days old, underwent three surgeries and nine rounds of chemotherapy, and now lives with cerebral palsy and visual impairments. Goodburn lives with three brain tumours himself.

lead.why: The freshest new item with the strongest corroboration across outlets, and a story a fan would share.

teams.heading: Alex Cuthbert overwhelmed in BBC commentary box as Wales beat All Blacks
teams.body: Former Wales wing Alex Cuthbert could barely speak when the final whistle sounded in Cardiff, and footage from the BBC Radio 5 Live commentary box shows him struggling to contain himself as the Principality Stadium erupted. "Oh my God, I don't know what to say. Wow, what?! Just unbelievable," he said. He singled out the second half, saying "The heart those boys showed, you could see it". The win ended 34 straight defeats to the All Blacks, a run stretching back to 1953.

teams.heading: Bautista Bernasconi starts at hooker and scores as Pumas injuries pile up
teams.body: Benetton hooker Bautista Bernasconi started against Italy after injuries to Julián Montoya, Ignacio Ruiz and Leonel Oviedo, and he made the most of the chance, driving over from a maul just before half-time to put the Pumas level at 7-7. The absences go further, with Thomas Gallo, Santiago Grondona, Marcos Kremer and Joaquín Oviedo also injured. Argentina still won 19-14, with Bernasconi's afternoon offering reassurance about the depth behind the first choice.

lead.why: The Genoa match report carries the most coverage, and its injury-forced hooker selection gives the day a fresh Argentina angle.

teams.heading: Carter Gordon recalled at flyhalf as Les Kiss restores Rob Valetini
teams.body: Les Kiss has restored Carter Gordon to the No 10 jersey for Sunday's Scotland test, the playmaker back from a broken leg, the latest of several injuries to derail his progress. Rob Valetini returns to six alongside Harry Wilson and Fraser McReight, while Declan Meredith, who looked lost against England, is dropped from the match-day 23. Seven different flyhalves have started since the last World Cup. "Carter will bring his flavour, he will bring his voice," Kiss said, with the Wallabies staring at a fourth straight Test defeat.

teams.heading: Japan had a player sent off before touching ball in Twickenham rout
teams.body: The 78-15 defeat to England at Allianz Stadium was shaped early: Japan were down to 14 men before they had touched the ball, and England led 32-3 inside 20 minutes. Gerard Meagher's Guardian analysis says the Brave Blossoms looked like amateurs against England's structures, which he reads as a sign of how wide the gap between teams has become. BBC Sport noted that Japan could not unlock the quick rucks and ball movement that have troubled bigger sides before.

lead.why: It is a new, Japan-focused item that avoids the Dearns co-captaincy story and the match report already on this tab.

teams.heading: Beauden Barrett says All Blacks hit Welsh "brick wall" in Cardiff
teams.body: Saturday's 28-35 loss in Cardiff was Wales's first win over the All Blacks since 1953, and Beauden Barrett, who captained New Zealand in a Test for the first time, said "It felt like a brick wall at times, so you have to give them credit." Wales made 346 tackles, with Dafydd Jenkins on 38, and held New Zealand up over the line three times in the second half to protect their seven-point lead. Wales scored five tries, a national record against New Zealand.

lead.why: A fresh first-hand reaction from Beauden Barrett to the Wales loss, not covered in the Rennie or Bunce pieces already run.

teams.heading: Nick Mallett says Springboks played into France's hands in 21-19 Paris defeat
teams.body: Former Bok coach Nick Mallett says the world champions were undone by their own approach, trailing 21-7 at half-time before losing 21-19 in Paris. Speaking on the Talking Boks podcast, he said the Boks lacked momentum early on. "We didn't play territory." Mallett said the Boks were running from inside their own 10-metre line and were tackled behind the advantage line too often, and that they tried to match France's game rather than impose their own. He argued the side must force set-piece after set-piece to create momentum.

lead.why: It is the only shortlist item framed around South Africa's own performance, and it gives a fresh, tactical angle on the Paris defeat without repeating the already-reported front-row and card stories.
